rewrite_premise.old_premise: 613 milestones drifted; need 10 units to reconcile (U-DRIFT-01..09 + 1 cron)
rewrite_premise.new_premise_for_ms4: Exactly 2 envelope rows drift (MF-MS1, MF-MS2, both FeasibilityEngine, both claim 'completed' but have shipped=0). MS4 is a narrow envelope-hygiene unit, not a roadmap reconciliation epic.

ms4_v2.title: Reconcile MF-MS1 and MF-MS2 envelopes via /envelope-sync
ms4_v2.spec: Run /envelope-sync MF-MS1 and /envelope-sync MF-MS2 in dry-run mode. Both envelopes currently claim status='completed' but have shipped=0/4 and 0/3 respectively. Two paths: (a) if FeasibilityEngine work is genuinely abandoned, flip envelope.status → 'not_started' and mark units accordingly; (b) if work is in flight on another branch, flip → 'in_progress' and leave units as 'pending'. Decision belongs to the FeasibilityEngine owner — this unit produces the patch JSON and a human review request, not autonomous --apply. Per envelope-sync.md L80 'Never auto-apply without user --apply flag and visual review.'
ms4_v2.acceptance: (1) /envelope-sync MF-MS1 --dry-run output written to state/shared/envelope-sync-MF-MS1.patch.json. (2) Same for MF-MS2. (3) PR-style comment in AGENT_CHAT.md tagging the FeasibilityEngine owner with the proposed status flip + decision-request. (4) After human approval, --apply commit lands and re-running scripts/build-milestone-progress.mjs reports totals.drift=0. (5) If owner unreachable for >48h, env tag 'envelope-stale' added to both envelopes and unit closes with status='deferred-to-owner-response' — NEVER autoflip.
ms4_v2.risk: low — only 2 envelopes; envelope-sync skill is dry-run by default

ms4_v2.title: Schedule drift-watch cron + alert on new drift
ms4_v2.spec: Register a cron that runs scripts/build-milestone-progress.mjs every 6h and posts an alert to AGENT_CHAT.md if totals.drift > 0 after the run. Today's baseline after U-DRIFT-01 should be 0. Use existing scheduling infrastructure (skills/cron-bootstrap, skills/cron-manage). Output: one-line summary 'drift: N (was 0 at T)'. If drift > 0, alert names the milestone and drift kind. This replaces the original U-DRIFT-02 (auto-flip false-negatives) which round 2 F-r2-a7-2 proved had zero data to operate on. The cron is monitoring, not auto-remediation — per F-r2-a7-4 cascade-risk finding, auto-flips remain manual.
ms4_v2.acceptance: (1) Cron registered via /cron-bootstrap or equivalent, fires every 6h. (2) MILESTONE_PROGRESS.json regenerated each fire. (3) AGENT_CHAT.md gets a post ONLY when drift > 0 (silent on drift=0 to avoid spam). (4) Cron writes its last-run telemetry to state/shared/drift-watch-cron.json with fields {lastRun, driftCount, milestonesAffected[]}. (5) Manual test: artificially create drift by patching one envelope, confirm cron fires alert within 6h, then revert.
ms4_v2.risk: low — read-only monitor, no envelope mutation
ms4_v2.optional_rationale: If MS4 ships within 1 day of U-DRIFT-01 closing and drift is already 0, the cron is nice-to-have but not blocking. Defer to backlog if MS5 (revenue work) has unmet capacity.

new_milestone_proposal.title: Revenue-cluster capability audit — verify SFC, Master Post, and CAM-bridge subsystems are revenue-grade (not just engine-present)
new_milestone_proposal.rationale: The original MS4 attempted to use envelope drift as a proxy for 'revenue clusters not yet shipped.' Round 2 proved that proxy is invalid (drift=2, neither row matches the SFC/Master-Post/CAM-bridge filter). The actual revenue question — 'do these subsystems expose billable, frontend-wired, dispatcher-reachable capability?' — needs a direct audit, not an envelope-reconciliation epic. ENGINE_DIGEST confirms the engines exist (E0265-E0271 Lathe Master Post family, E0321-E0322 MasterPost AGI, E0337 WEDM Master Post, E0355 Okuma B250, E0182 Hurco V11). Whether each is wired to a dispatcher, exposed via a frontend page, and gated by a billable boundary is the open question. This milestone surfaces those gaps without conflating them with envelope hygiene.
new_milestone_proposal.premise_basis: Direct evidence from ENGINE_DIGEST + BUILD_STATE.needs_wiring + BUILD_STATE.needs_frontend — NOT envelope drift.
depends_on: U-DRIFT-01 (closes envelope noise so audit results aren't polluted)
blocks: REVENUE-MS1 billing/tier gating — must know what's revenue-grade before gating it

units.title: Audit SpecificCuttingEnergyEngine + speed/feed engine family for stub returns and dispatcher wiring
units.spec: Enumerate every engine in src/engines/ matching SpecificCuttingEnergy|SpeedFeed|CuttingForce|Kienzle. For each: (a) check it has a non-stub run()/calc() implementation (no 'return 0' or 'TODO' bodies — use the always-build-guard.mjs heuristic), (b) confirm it's wired to prism_calc dispatcher (grep camDispatcher.ts + calcDispatcher.ts), (c) confirm at least one test file asserts a non-trivial numeric result. Report goes to state/shared/audit-findings/revenue-roadmap/round3-audit-sfc.json with one row per engine and a {wired, stubbed, tested} verdict.
units.acceptance: (1) Audit JSON lists every SFC-family engine with verdicts. (2) Every engine has dispatcher_action_count > 0 OR is explicitly tagged WIRE-EXEMPT with a wrapper reference (per CLAUDE.md engine wiring rule). (3) Stubs flagged with severity (high if it's the canonical SFC engine, low if it's a deprecated variant). (4) Output cross-referenced with BUILD_STATE.needs_wiring to confirm no SFC engine is in needs_wiring without an explanation. (5) Recent commit 9386a4e88 [U-WIRE-CALC-SCE] is sanity-checked — that wiring should show up in the audit as a recent fix.

units.title: Verify Master Post controller-dialect coverage and dispatcher exposure
units.spec: ENGINE_DIGEST shows ~11 Master Post engines spanning Lathe (E0265-E0271), AGI (E0321-E0322), WEDM (E0337), Okuma (E0355), and Hurco V11 (E0182). For each: (a) identify the target controller dialect, (b) verify a sample post-output file exists in JM DIE/ that the engine handles, (c) confirm at least one dispatcher (prism_cam, camDispatcher) exposes a 'generate post' or equivalent action that routes to this engine. Gap list: dialects with NO engine (e.g. is there a Mazak Smart H4 post for the lathe family?). Output: state/shared/audit-findings/revenue-roadmap/round3-audit-masterpost.json with rows {engine, dialect, sampleProgramTested, dispatcherWired, frontendExposed}.
units.acceptance: (1) Audit JSON enumerates all 11+ Master Post engines with dialect mapping. (2) Each row has a JM DIE/ sample program path proving the engine round-trips real shop data (per JM Die test shop directive in CLAUDE.md). (3) Dialect-gap list explicit — every shop controller in shop-configuration must have an engine OR a justified deferral. (4) For at least one dialect with frontendExposed=false, a wiring task is filed in BUILD_STATE.needs_frontend with priority=revenue.

units.title: CAM-bridge inventory — Fusion 360, hyperMILL, Mastercam, ESPRIT, Inventor, SolidWorks
units.spec: Six external CAM systems need bridges per the original MS4 cluster list. For each: (a) does a bridge engine exist (e.g. FusionBridgeEngine, HyperMILLBridgeEngine — confirmed in ENGINE_DIGEST? Round 2 didn't search; this unit does), (b) is it dispatcher-wired (prism_cam vendor action or dedicated dispatcher), (c) does it have a smoke test that exercises a real add-in handshake (HTTP, file-watch, COM, etc.), (d) is the add-in/plugin shipped to a discoverable location (CAM-vendor extension store, mcp-server/web/cam-bridges/, etc.)? Output: state/shared/audit-findings/revenue-roadmap/round3-audit-cam-bridges.json with one row per vendor and a readiness score.
units.acceptance: (1) Six bridge rows present. (2) For each existing bridge, one E2E smoke test path documented and CI-runnable. (3) For each missing bridge, a one-paragraph build plan (engine name, dispatcher action, minimum add-in surface). (4) Cowork-connectors skill cross-referenced — if a bridge is listed there but not in src/engines, that's a documentation drift filed as a finding. (5) Existing Cowork connector list (cowork-connectors skill) used as ground-truth for vendor priority ordering.

units.title: Synthesize the three audits into a single revenue-cluster gap report
units.spec: Combine the three audit JSONs above into state/shared/audit-findings/revenue-roadmap/round3-revenue-cluster-gaps.md. For each cluster (SFC, Master Post, CAM bridges), list: (a) what ships TODAY at revenue grade (dispatcher-wired + frontend-reachable + billable-able), (b) what is engine-only (needs wiring/frontend), (c) what is missing entirely. This report becomes input to REVENUE-MS1 billing/tier gating — you cannot gate what does not exist as a complete surface.
units.acceptance: (1) Single markdown report with 3 cluster sections. (2) Each cluster has a {ships, needs_wiring, missing} tally. (3) Report references BUILD_STATE.json and ENGINE_DIGEST.md by line/row — auditable, no fabricated counts. (4) Filed under round3 audit-findings, available for round-4 cross-validation by another agent.

summary.verdict: MS4 v2 is a 2-unit envelope-hygiene closure (U-DRIFT-01 reconciles MF-MS1/MF-MS2 via dry-run /envelope-sync + human approval, U-DRIFT-02 optional cron monitor). The conflated revenue-cluster work splits cleanly into a separate REVENUE-SUPPORT-AUDIT-MS5 (4 units: SFC audit, Master Post audit, CAM-bridge audit, synthesis). This separates envelope hygiene (small, mechanical, dry-run-gated) from revenue-grade capability audit (engine-by-engine, dispatcher-wired, frontend-reachable). Total 6 units replaces the unjustified 10. No autonomous envelope mutation. Premise of each unit is direct evidence (MILESTONE_PROGRESS.drift, ENGINE_DIGEST entries, BUILD_STATE blocks), not derived from a false drift count.
summary.one_line: MS4 v2: 2 units (real drift=2, not 613); REVENUE-SUPPORT-AUDIT-MS5: 4 units (the actual revenue-cluster audit work).
